candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the contents of a ZIP archive (entry names are fully attacker-defined); control of the archive is not derived from any in-repo input source. Impact occurs whenever code executing in the instrumented JVM (a plugin built against one-java-agent-plugin, or any consumer of this public library method) calls IOUtils.unzip on an attacker-influenced archive.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified in source that the method is dead code within this snapshot: literal search for 'unzip' returns only IOUtils.java and Maven Ant tasks in poms; the P1 relation trace for IOUtils.unzip shows only intra-class callees (close overloads), no callers. The class is public and shipped in the one-java-agent-plugin library module, so external/plugin callers are plausible but not evidenced here. Also checked that no other path/exec/deserialization sink exists in the Java sources (no Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, no ObjectInputStream, no URLConnection besides the Maven wrapper), which makes this the only canonical injection sink in the tree.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write/overwrite with the privileges of the JVM running the extraction (e.g., escaping the extraction directory into application config, scripts, or classpath locations): data tampering/denial of service and potential code execution depending on the writable target path. No confidentiality or network impact by itself.
candidates.prerequisites: A caller must invoke the public static IOUtils.unzip(String, String) on an untrusted/attacker-influenced archive, and the JVM must have write permission to the resolved target paths. No caller exists anywhere in this snapshot (searched the whole tree), so this is a latent vulnerable primitive rather than a demonstrated path.
candidates.root_cause: IOUtils.unzip(String zipFile, String extractFolder) (lines 106-161) takes each entry name (line 122) and builds the destination with new File(newPath, currentEntry) (line 124), then creates the parent directories with destinationParent.mkdirs() (line 129) and writes the entry content with new FileOutputStream(destFile) (line 141). There is no canonicalization or containment check (no getCanonicalPath/getCanonicalFile anywhere in the repository), so archive entry names containing '../' (or otherwise crafted path fragments) resolve outside extractFolder. The utility exposes only two unrelated helpers (copy/close) besides unzip, i.e., the missing validation is in this method itself, not in a caller.
candidates.title: Zip Slip path traversal in IOUtils.unzip: unvalidated ZipEntry name is used as destination path (arbitrary file write)
candidates.trace: unzip (IOUtils.java:106) -> new ZipFile(file) (112) -> zip.entries() (116) -> zipFileEntries.nextElement() (121) -> entry.getName() (122) -> new File(newPath, currentEntry) (124) -> destinationParent.mkdirs() (129) -> new FileOutputStream(destFile) (141) -> dest.write(data, 0, currentByte) (146). No path normalization or prefix check intervenes; repository-wide search found no getCanonical* usage and no unzip call site (only Maven Ant's <unzip> in one-java-agent/pom.xml, which is unrelated to this method).
candidates.unverified: Runtime reachability and exploitability are not confirmed; no caller of IOUtils.unzip exists in the reviewed snapshot, and no test sources are present. Whether any external consumer passes an attacker-controlled archive is unknown. The finding is a source-evidence lead, not a proven vulnerability.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') / Zip Slip; CWE-73 External Control of File Name or Path

coverage_summary: Scope: 102 model-visible files (79 Java). All Java sources were inspected; the agent core (BootstrapAgent, AgentImpl, BootstrapAgent/NopAgent, AgentSpyImpl, ClassLoader_Instrument, InstrumentationUtils), plugin system (PluginManagerImpl, OneAgentPlugin, TraditionalPlugin, PlguinClassLoader, PluginConfigImpl, TraditionalPluginConfigImpl, PropertiesInjectUtils), services (ComponentManagerImpl, TransformerManagerImpl, OneAgentClassFileTransformer, ClassLoaderHandlerManagerImpl), utils (IOUtils, FeatureCodec, JarUtils, PropertiesUtils, AnsiLog, OSUtils, ObjectUtils, StringUtils) and the copied Spring env package were read in full or by exhaustive sink/signature search. Build/config read: root/module poms, .github workflows, oneagent-logback.xml, assembly.xml and plugin.properties files, mvnw.cmd, .mvn/wrapper files. P1 index: 101/102 files indexed, 79 Java parsed, 0 parse errors, 1 non-Java file missing, 1206 unresolved calls, no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution; it was used only for navigation and every used edge was verified against source text (e.g., confirming IOUtils.unzip and PropertiesInjectUtils have no in-repo callers).
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, and the Java sources of demo-agent, demo-plugin and dubbo-test-plugin are absent (only pom/assembly/plugin.properties), so plugin-activator and ClassLoaderHandler implementations that could call utilities such as IOUtils.unzip or PropertiesInjectUtilsInject could not be inspected.
Static review only: no code was built or executed; runtime reachability, data flow and exploitability were not confirmed, and candidates are leads, not confirmed vulnerabilities.

The P1 relation index has no data-flow/control-flow and leaves 1206 calls unresolved; unreported index absence is not evidence that an area is safe (Spring annotation/DI hints and the missing non-Java index file were not verified).
Dependency versions (logback 1.2.3, slf4j 1.7.25, bytekit 0.0.5, spring-boot-starter-test 1.5.9) were not assessed for known CVEs; no external lookups or CVE checks were performed per instructions.
The scope covers only this snapshot; behavior of consumer code (plugins, downstream users of one-java-agent-plugin) is outside the evidence and is exactly the gap for the submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Untrusted/attacker-writable plugin code execution: AgentImpl.init loads plugins from <oneagent.home>/plugins and from the comma-separated oneagent.extPlugins argument (AgentImpl.java:145-173), PluginManagerImpl.loadPlugin loads every subdirectory containing plugin.properties (PluginManagerImpl.java:77-126), OneAgentPlugin reflects a pluginActivator class (OneAgentPlugin.java:96-98), and TraditionalPlugin reflectively invokes premain/agentmain and calls instrumentation.appendToSystemClassLoaderSearch / creates a URLClassLoader for the plugin jar (TraditionalPlugin.java:77-114) with no integrity or permission checks.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the documented purpose of the project (plugin/traditional-agent loader), and the plugin directory/arguments come from the JVM launch configuration or the agent jar location, i.e., from the operator who already controls JVM startup. No source evidence in the snapshot shows a lower-privileged writer into those directories, so this is a design/hardening observation rather than a demonstrated vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Maven Wrapper bootstrap download without integrity verification: .mvn/wrapper/MavenWrapperDownloader.java:97-115 downloads wrapperUrl from .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties and writes/executes it; mvnw.cmd:123-155 downloads maven-wrapper-0.5.6.jar (overridable via MVNW_REPOURL) and later runs it with java -classpath, with no checksum/signature check.
rejected_leads.reason: Third-party Maven-wrapper boilerplate (takari 0.5.6), not project logic; the configured/default URLs are HTTPS to repo.maven.apache.org, and override via wrapperUrl/MVNW_REPOURL or TLS interception already implies control over the developer/build environment. Kept as a hardening note, not a candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflective property injection: PropertiesInjectUtils.inject parses config values into typed values and invokes setters (PropertiesInjectUtils.java:80-131) while ComponentManagerImpl.inject sets private fields via setAccessible (ComponentManagerImpl.java:81-99).
rejected_leads.reason: No in-repo caller of PropertiesInjectUtils (relation trace and text search show only self-recursion); values originate from local plugin.properties/system properties and the target object classes are developer-defined, so there is no attacker-controlled target/invocation and no in-snapshot data flow to an impact.

rejected_leads.lead: Parent-last class loading in PlguinClassLoader (PlguinClassLoader.java:18-38) lets plugin jars shadow any non-java./sun. class.
rejected_leads.reason: Affects only the plugin's own class loader and the plugin is trusted, operator-installed code by design; no untrusted code path or cross-tenant boundary is shown in the snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Agent arguments are URL-decoded (AgentImpl.decodeArg, AgentImpl.java:224-233) and parsed by FeatureCodec into filesystem paths (oneagent.home, oneagent.extPlugins) used for plugin loading.
rejected_leads.reason: The argument string is supplied with the -javaagent JVM option, so decoding only transforms the operator's own input; no untrusted source reaches this code.

rejected_leads.lead: CI workflow injection/checkout of untrusted code (.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml, test.yaml).
rejected_leads.reason: Evaluated; both workflows use push/pull_request with actions/checkout of the repository under test, no pull_request_target or secrets exposure pattern was found.

summary: Reviewed the snapshot of alibaba/one-java-agent (a Java-agent plugin framework): 102 files in scope, 79 Java files, plus all build/config files. The codebase contains no network, command-execution, or deserialization sinks, and no attacker-reachable path into agent internals from remote input; the plugin/traditional-agent loading model is the product's core (trusted, operator-controlled) feature. The strongest source-evident defect is a classic Zip Slip in the public utility com.alibaba.oneagent.utils.IOUtils.unzip: ZipEntry names are joined to the extraction directory and written without any normalization/containment check, so a crafted archive can write outside the intended folder. Its weakness as a finding is that this snapshot contains no in-repo caller, so reachability is unproven; I therefore submit it only as a low-confidence candidate, with the other themes listed as rejected leads.
